cards.heading: Sync deletion semantics: definition
cards.question: Why is deletion described as the hardest part of mirroring external sources in continuous sync?
cards.answer: Items disappear through at least six distinct channels, bounded and unbounded collections need opposite deletion strategies, and every wrong choice fails silently rather than loudly.

cards.heading: Manifest-diff vs full-rescan deletion
cards.question: When is manifest-diff deletion correct, and when is full-rescan tombstoning correct?
cards.answer: Manifest-diff (remove what the latest listing omits) is correct for bounded collections. Full-rescan tombstoning (mark dead what a complete walk never saw) is correct for unbounded streams. Each is destructive when applied to the other's data shape.

cards.heading: Misapplying manifest-diff deletion
cards.question: What happens if manifest-diff deletion is applied to a cursored stream instead of a bounded collection?
cards.answer: It wipes all history below the watermark.

cards.heading: Misapplying full-rescan tombstoning
cards.question: What happens if full-rescan tombstoning is applied to a bounded collection instead of an unbounded stream?
cards.answer: It wastes enormous work — a full walk to detect deletions that a manifest diff would find directly.

cards.heading: The failure mode of wrong deletion strategy
cards.question: What is the signature failure when a deletion channel is missed or the wrong strategy is used?
cards.answer: Silent wrongness, not an error — e.g. a mirror that confidently describes a table dropped months ago.

cards.heading: Six deletion channels
cards.question: Name the six channels through which an item can disappear from a source in continuous sync.
cards.answer: Source confirms removal; a parent's manifest stops listing a child; a cursored record expires; a stale probe 404s; a full re-walk completes without seeing an item; a user disconnects a source.
